-- Ports prepare_crime_db.py assign_zones(), including its nearest-zone snap.
-- The snap is a real business rule, not an implementation detail: edge-street
-- geocodes on Harlem, Austin and North Ave land just outside the village polygon
-- and would otherwise be dropped. Omitting it moves 1627 rows.
with pts as (

    select
        record_id,
        lat,
        long,
        case when lat is not null then ST_Point(long, lat) end as pt
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes"

), candidates as (

    select
        p.record_id,
        z.zone_id,
        z.zone_name,
        ST_Contains(z.zone_geom, p.pt) as contained,
        ST_Distance(p.pt, z.zone_geom) as dist
    from pts as p
    cross join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_policing_zones" as z
    where p.pt is not null

), best as (

    select
        record_id,
        zone_id,
        zone_name,
        contained,
        dist,
        count(*) filter (where contained) over (partition by record_id) as contain_count
    from candidates
    qualify row_number() over (
        partition by record_id
        order by contained desc, dist asc, zone_id asc
    ) = 1

)

select
    p.record_id,
    p.lat,
    p.long,
    case when b.contained or b.dist < 0.0005 then b.zone_id   end as zone_id,
    case when b.contained or b.dist < 0.0005 then b.zone_name end as zone_name,
    coalesce(b.contain_count, 0) > 1 as zone_boundary_ambiguous,
    case
        when p.lat is null                                   then 'ungeocoded'
        when b.contained                                     then 'in_village'
        when b.dist < 0.0005   then 'snapped'
        else 'outside_village'
    end as zone_status

from pts as p
left join best as b using (record_id)

-- Same incident ingested twice because OPPD republished the report under a new
-- filename (-v2 against -v3, or an -02 suffix). Currently 45 groups, 48 rows
-- double counted downstream. Flagged not fixed: the repair belongs in
-- drop_exact_source_duplicates. See dbt_writeup.md.

select
    complaint_num,
    count(*)                                 as row_count,
    string_agg(distinct pdf_filename, ' | ') as filenames

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."crimes"
where complaint_num is not null
group by complaint_num
having count(*) > 1
   and count(distinct date) = 1
   and count(distinct offense) = 1
   and count(distinct location) = 1
   and count(distinct pdf_filename) > 1

-- Flags republication double counts without dropping them. Removing rows here
-- would change published counts silently; downstream picks the filter.
-- Highest filename sorts last for the -v2/-v3 and -02 suffix conventions.
with ranked as (

    select
        c.*,
        q.quality_class,
        case
            when q.quality_class = 'republished'
            then row_number() over (
                partition by c.complaint_num
                order by c.pdf_filename desc
            )
            else 1
        end as republication_rank
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes" as c
    left join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_complaint_quality" as q
        on c.complaint_num = q.complaint_num

)

select
    *,
    republication_rank > 1 as is_duplicate_republication
from ranked

select record_id
from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_crimes_deduplicated"
where record_id is null

select
    record_id as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_crimes_deduplicated"
where record_id is not null
group by record_id
having count(*) > 1

-- Geometry is dropped here; parquet has no native GEOMETRY type and no consumer
-- needs the polygon, only the label.
select
    z.zone_id,
    z.zone_name,
    count(c.record_id) as incident_count

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_policing_zones" as z
left join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_crimes_zoned" as c
    on c.zone_id = z.zone_id
group by z.zone_id, z.zone_name

-- Does the SQL agree with the Python it reimplements?
--
-- One rule in this project exists twice. assign_zones() in prepare_crime_db.py
-- assigns each incident to a policing zone and stores the answer in
-- crimes.parquet; int_crimes_zoned recomputes it from the polygons with
-- ST_Contains and the same snap tolerance. Two implementations of one rule is a
-- liability unless something compares them, so this does.
--
-- It is a value check, not a count check. The row counts would agree perfectly
-- even if every incident landed in the wrong zone, because the same rows come out
-- either way. Only comparing the assignments catches a real divergence, which is
-- the kind that appears when someone tunes SNAP_TOL in the Python and nothing
-- tells the SQL.
--
-- Twenty rows are expected to disagree and are excluded from the failure
-- condition rather than from the count. Zone polygons share edges, so a point on a
-- boundary is genuinely inside two of them. This project breaks the tie on the
-- lowest zone_id; the pipeline breaks it differently. Both answers are defensible,
-- neither is wrong, and int_crimes_zoned flags every such row as
-- zone_boundary_ambiguous so the disagreement stays visible instead of being
-- quietly absorbed.

with compared as (
    select
        p.record_id,
        p.zone_id as pipeline_zone_id,
        d.zone_id as dbt_zone_id,
        d.zone_boundary_ambiguous,
        p.zone_id is not distinct from d.zone_id as agrees
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."stg_crimes" as p
    join "opcrime_dbt"."main"."int_crimes_zoned" as d using (record_id)
),

rolled as (
    select
        count(*) as rows_compared,
        count(*) filter (where agrees) as assignments_agree,
        count(*) filter (where not agrees) as assignments_differ,
        count(*) filter (where not agrees and zone_boundary_ambiguous)
            as differ_on_shared_boundary,
        count(*) filter (where not agrees and not zone_boundary_ambiguous)
            as differ_unexplained,
        count(*) filter (where pipeline_zone_id is null and dbt_zone_id is not null)
            as dbt_assigned_pipeline_did_not,
        count(*) filter (where pipeline_zone_id is not null and dbt_zone_id is null)
            as pipeline_assigned_dbt_did_not
    from compared
)

select 'zone_rows_compared' as measure, 'count' as check_kind,
       rows_compared::double as value, 0.0 as expected,
       'Incidents where both implementations produced an answer to compare.' as detail
from rolled
union all
select 'zone_assignments_agree', 'count', assignments_agree::double, rows_compared::double,
       'Incidents where the SQL and the Python chose the same zone, null included.'
from rolled
union all
select 'zone_match_rate_pct', 'value',
       round(assignments_agree * 100.0 / nullif(rows_compared, 0), 3), 100.0,
       'Agreement rate. Expected to sit just under 100 because of the shared-boundary ties.'
from rolled
union all
select 'zone_differ_on_shared_boundary', 'count', differ_on_shared_boundary::double, 0.0,
       'Disagreements on points inside two polygons at once. Expected, flagged, and not a defect.'
from rolled
union all
select 'zone_differ_unexplained', 'count', differ_unexplained::double, 0.0,
       'Disagreements with no boundary ambiguity to explain them. Must be zero: anything here means the two implementations have actually drifted.'
from rolled
union all
select 'zone_dbt_assigned_pipeline_did_not', 'count', dbt_assigned_pipeline_did_not::double, 0.0,
       'The SQL placed an incident in a zone the Python left unassigned. A tolerance difference would show up here first.'
from rolled
union all
select 'zone_pipeline_assigned_dbt_did_not', 'count', pipeline_assigned_dbt_did_not::double, 0.0,
       'The Python placed an incident the SQL left unassigned. The other direction of the same drift.'
from rolled

-- Measures how well the dbt-side naive join key matches the shared geocode cache.
-- It does NOT measure whether the pipeline resolved an address: 15,431 rows that
-- this join fails to match are geocoded perfectly well, because the pipeline keys
-- on normalize_location() output while dbt only has lower(trim(location)).
--
-- The operational geocode signal is pipeline_has_coords. The naive key exists to
-- quantify what publishing a real location_key upstream would buy.
select
    c.record_id,
    c.source,
    c.location,
    c.location_key_naive,
    c.lat  as pipeline_lat,
    c.long as pipeline_long,
    g.lat  as cache_lat,
    g.long as cache_long,
    case
        when g.location_key is null then 'unmatched'
        when g.known_unresolvable   then 'cached_unresolvable'
        else 'matched'
    end as naive_key_status,
    c.lat is not null as pipeline_has_coords

    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"

    union all
    select 'outside_village',
           'Geocoded outside the village. Correct: OPPD reports incidents in neighbouring towns',
           count(*) filter (where zone_status = 'outside_village'), count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"

    union all
    select 'pdf_only',
           'Present in the PDF activity reports only, so no NIBRS coding or exact timestamp',
           count(*) filter (where source = 'pdf'), count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"

    union all
    select 'dashboard_only',
           'Present in the Power BI export only, so no narrative text',
           count(*) filter (where source = 'dashboard'), count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"

    union all
    select 'both_sources',
           'Matched across both ingest streams and merged',
           count(*) filter (where source = 'both'), count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"

)

select
    measure,
    description,
    row_count,
    round(100.0 * row_count / denominator, 2) as pct_of_rows
from checks
order by row_count desc

select
    offense,
    primary_crime_against,
    strftime(date, '%Y-%m')       as year_month,
    year(date)                    as year,
    count(*)                      as incident_count,
    count(distinct zone_id)       as zones_touched,
    count(*) filter (where zone_status = 'outside_village') as outside_village_count

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
where date > '1901-01-01'
  and offense is not null
group by offense, primary_crime_against, year_month, year

-- Actual defects only. Expected characteristics of the data live in
-- data_profile_summary: a row whose owner reads "not a defect" does not belong in
-- a defect table, and mixing the two buries the real numbers under large
-- harmless ones.
with checks as (

    select 'republished_pdf_rows' as issue,
           'Same incident ingested twice under a revised PDF filename' as description,
           'ingest bug, fix in drop_exact_source_duplicates' as owner,
           count(*) as row_count
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where is_duplicate_republication

    union all
    select 'complaint_collisions',
           'One complaint number on materially different incidents',
           'source data, flag only',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where complaint_quality_class = 'collision'

    union all
    select 'ungeocoded',
           'No coordinates resolved',
           'run a Python cache-fill',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where lat is null

    union all
    select 'date_sentinel',
           'Date failed to parse and fell back to 1900-01-01',
           'source data, flag only',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where date <= '1901-01-01'

    union all
    select 'date_future',
           'Incident date is in the future',
           'source data, poisons naive freshness checks',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where date > current_date

    union all
    select 'pdf_dashboard_date_mismatch',
           'PDF and dashboard disagree on the incident date by a day or more',
           'flagged in merge_notes, not repaired',
           count(*)
    from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
    where date_mismatch

)

select
    issue,
    description,
    owner,
    row_count,
    round(100.0 * row_count / (select count(*) from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"), 2) as pct_of_rows
from checks
order by row_count desc

select
    zone_id,
    zone_name,
    zone_status,
    strftime(date, '%Y-%m')                     as year_month,
    year(date)                                  as year,
    month(date)                                 as month,
    count(*)                                    as incident_count,
    count(*) filter (where not is_duplicate_republication) as deduplicated_count,
    count(distinct complaint_num)               as distinct_complaints,
    count(*) filter (where primary_crime_against = 'Person')   as crimes_against_person,
    count(*) filter (where primary_crime_against = 'Property') as crimes_against_property,
    count(*) filter (where primary_crime_against = 'Society')  as crimes_against_society

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."fct_incidents"
where date > '1901-01-01'
group by zone_id, zone_name, zone_status, year_month, year, month

select measure
from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."data_profile_summary"
where measure is null

select
    measure as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."data_profile_summary"
where measure is not null
group by measure
having count(*) > 1

select issue
from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."data_quality_summary"
where issue is null

select row_count
from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."data_quality_summary"
where row_count is null

select
    issue as unique_field,
    count(*) as n_records

from "opcrime_dbt"."main"."data_quality_summary"
where issue is not null
group by issue
having count(*) > 1
